propositions: The N=3000 import benchmark currently invokes git config user.name 6,001 times (once per envelope in append_event) consuming 47.79s, when the author value should be constant across a single import operation.

The batch_stage_and_commit path calls sweep_stale_staging once per new CREATE ticket (3,000 times in the benchmark) rather than once per batch, rescanning the same staging root while earlier prepared items remain unpublished and consuming 15.94s.

An explicit import-scoped author cache and at-most-once-per-batch stale staging sweep can eliminate 60.8s (78.8% of current 77.2s bulk-path time) while preserving all crash-safety, rollback, idempotency, and 24-commit guarantees.
Interactive and direct stage_event calls must retain live author lookup and per-write stale sweep behavior; cache and batch optimizations must not leak across independent operations or contexts.

The optimization must be validated by holding out a deterministic oracle that records exactly one user.name lookup and 12 stale sweeps (half the expected commit count for N=3000) without timing thresholds, and independently demonstrating that removing each optimization mechanism returns the oracle to RED.
